title: Minivan plunges into ravine on Highway 304
detail: Khaosod English reports a passenger minivan left the road at km 243 and rolled into a ravine; police attributed it to driver fatigue.

title: New Year 'seven dangerous days' road toll: 272 dead
detail: DDPM reported 1,511 crashes, 272 deaths and 1,464 injuries over the 30 Dec 2025–5 Jan 2026 holiday campaign; Bangkok had the most deaths (22), per The Nation.
agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

title: Tour speedboat sinks after collision with trawler off Koh Khiao
detail: A tour speedboat carrying about 55 people collided with a fishing trawler between Phuket and Koh Phi Phi and sank; one foreign tourist died and 22 were injured, per Thai Examiner. The operator was detained.
agency: Maritime Security Command Region 3; Marine Department

title: Construction crane falls on express train at Sikhio
detail: A launching gantry for the Bangkok–Nong Khai high-speed rail project collapsed onto express train No. 21 (Bangkok–Ubon Ratchathani) near km 220, derailing it. Wikipedia lists 30 dead and 69 injured; Northeastern Line services resumed normally on 24 January.
place: Ban Thanon Khot, railway km 220 between Nong Nam Khun and Sikhio stations
agency: State Railway of Thailand; Department of Rail Transport

title: Crane and girder collapse on Rama II elevated motorway works
detail: A launching gantry and concrete segment fell from the M82 elevated motorway project near the Tha Chin River bridge, crushing two vehicles; The Nation reported 2 dead and 5 injured, with heavy congestion both ways.
place: Rama II Road near Tha Chin River bridge ascent, Tha Chin subdistrict

title: Sinkhole swallows pickup on inbound Rama II Road
detail: The inbound road surface collapsed near the Big Song shopping centre, and a pickup fell in; officials suspected a burst water main. The section was closed, causing heavy congestion both ways, according to The Nation.
place: Rama II Road inbound near Big Song shopping centre

title: Highways Dept closes Rama II main road for 60 days after crane collapse
detail: The Department of Highways said it would close the affected Rama II main road section in the M82 project area for 60 days and reviewed ending the contract, according to The Nation.
place: Rama II Road, Bang Khun Thian–Ban Phaeo motorway project section

title: Check-in system fault causes long queues at Suvarnabhumi
detail: Thaiger reports Thai Airways' self-service kiosks could not print bag tags after a new baggage policy took effect, pushing passengers to staffed counters and creating long queues.

title: Hauliers threaten nationwide stoppage over diesel crisis, cite Laem Chabang delays
detail: The Land Transport Federation of Thailand demanded a diesel price cap and cutting truck turnaround at Laem Chabang Port to 3–4 hours per trip. It warned of a nationwide transport suspension if ignored, per The Nation.

title: Songkran 'seven dangerous days' road toll: 242 dead
detail: DDPM reported 1,242 crashes, 242 deaths and 1,200 injuries over 10–16 April; Bangkok had the most deaths (21), and speeding and motorcycles dominated, per The Nation.
agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

title: Nine killed as pickup overturns on steep Nan mountain road
detail: A family pickup lost control on a downhill bend at km 8+700 of the Pua–Bo Kluea road and overturned, killing nine (including children) and injuring 14, per The Nation.

title: Thai–Cambodian land border stays shut into 10th month
detail: The Nation reported that land crossings with Cambodia had been closed since 23 June 2025. Officials said they were unlikely to reopen in 2026, which hit cross-border traffic and trade.
place: Thai–Cambodian land border (Chanthaburi, Trat, Surin, Ubon Ratchathani crossings)

title: Pratunam flyover shut ~10 months for Orange Line works
detail: MRTA closed the Pratunam flyover on Phetchaburi Road from 24 April 2026 to 11 February 2027 for underground Orange Line works and published five detour routes, per The Nation.
agency: Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand

title: Border gate stays shut at Khlong Luek, stranding repatriation of 635 Thais
detail: Khaosod English reports that Cambodian officials at Poipet kept the gate at the Friendship Bridge crossing closed without explanation, delaying the handover of 635 Thai nationals.
place: Khlong Luek checkpoint, Thai–Cambodian Friendship Bridge

title: Tour bus crash on rain-slick Highway 304 injures 35
detail: A tour bus collided with a truck and a pickup on a steep, curving section and left the road; The Nation reported 35 injured, one critically, and no deaths.

title: Freight train hits city bus at Makkasan crossing; bus burns
detail: A freight train from Chachoengsao struck a BMTA route 23 bus at the crossing near Airport Rail Link Makkasan station and dragged it about 50 m; the bus caught fire. Khaosod English reported 8 killed and more than 20 injured.
place: Level crossing near Makkasan station, Asok–Din Daeng Road
agency: State Railway of Thailand; BMTA; DDPM

title: Boulders block Highway 108 in Mae Hong Son, vehicles stranded
detail: A landslide dropped boulders across both directions at km 301 (Mae Surin section); they were too large for local equipment, and many vehicles were stranded, per Thaiger.

title: Four killed in pickup–sedan collision in Wiang Chai
detail: A pickup and a sedan collided at the Ban Ling Kunchon traffic-light junction; four died and one was critically injured, per Chiang Rai Times.
place: Ban Ling Kunchon intersection, Don Sila

title: Factory shuttle bus rams school transport, 24 students hurt
detail: On the first day of term a factory shuttle bus hit the rear of a school transport vehicle on Road 3079; 24 students were injured, five moderately, per Khaosod English.
place: Road 3079 near housing estate, Tha Tum subdistrict

title: Hat Yai runway closed after fire-engine accident
detail: Hat Yai International Airport closed Runway 26 from 13:55 to 16:30 after an airport fire engine accident; two inbound flights diverted to Krabi, per The Nation.

title: Double-decker coach hits parked lorry on Highway 201, 15 hurt
detail: An overnight coach from Bangkok's Mo Chit terminal crashed into an 18-wheel lorry parked on the roadside, injuring 15, per Khaosod English.

title: Construction barge capsizes off Samut Prakan pier
detail: Khaosod English reports that a construction barge overturned near a private pier opposite Suk Sawat Soi 84, leaving two people in the water; the cause was under investigation.
place: Chao Phraya River opposite Suk Sawat Soi 84

title: Roads closed after water floods Purple Line tunnel shaft
detail: MRTA closed all lanes of Prajadhipok Road between Ban Khaek and Wongwian Yai after groundwater entered a South Purple Line construction shaft, per Khaosod English.
agency: Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand

title: Chiang Rai city road closed for flood-damage repairs
detail: Highway 1232 from King Mengrai Monument to the Nong Bua junction was closed from 10 July to 20 September to rebuild a storm-weakened road base, per Chiang Rai Times.
place: Highway 1232, King Mengrai Monument–Nong Bua junction
agency: Department of Highways (Chiang Rai Highway District 1)

title: Thai AirAsia pulls nine domestic routes from Suvarnabhumi
detail: Thai AirAsia suspended nine domestic routes from Suvarnabhumi from 15 July to 30 September, moving them to Don Mueang. The Nation said high fuel costs and weak demand were the reasons.

title: School bus overturns in Surin, 57 hurt
detail: A school bus from Khukhan (Sisaket) lost control and overturned in front of Wat Taluak; 51 students and 6 teachers had minor injuries, per Khaosod English.
place: Highway 214 in front of Wat Taluak, Kang Aen subdistrict

title: Airport Rail Link car derails at Khlong Tan depot
detail: A car derailed at switch 3018 while entering the depot at 00:47, leaving one train in service that morning. SRT added trains and shuttle buses between Makkasan and Suvarnabhumi, per The Nation.
agency: State Railway of Thailand; Department of Rail Transport

title: Airport Rail Link runs single-track at 30-minute intervals
detail: Technical issues forced single-track running with a train every 30 minutes, adding about 30 minutes from Phaya Thai to Suvarnabhumi. Free shuttle buses ran between Makkasan and the airport, per The Nation.

title: Longtail tour boat capsizes in big swell off Ao Nang
detail: A wave capsized a longtail carrying 10 tourists near Laem Hang Nak; all 12 aboard were rescued, with 6 minor injuries, per Thai Examiner.
place: Near Laem Hang Nak, between Ao Nang and Hong Island
agency: Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park

title: Flash floods in Nan collapse bridge on Pua–Bo Kluea route
detail: Over 200mm of rain caused floods in several Nan districts; a bridge on Highway 1256 (Pua–Bo Kluea) collapsed and the Phayaeng–Kiew Muang road became impassable, per Khaosod English.

title: Nan floods close roads and a city bridge
detail: The Nation reported that Route 1256 was closed after power poles fell, Woranakhon Road in Tha Wang Pha was impassable and Nakhon Nan Pattana Bridge was scheduled to close. The same report put the flood toll at two dead.
place: Tha Wang Pha market and Nan town

title: Thousands of flight delays at Bangkok airports over three days
detail: AirHelp reported 2,316 delays and 143 cancellations at Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang on 21–23 August. It attributed them to heavy traffic, tight ground-handling buffers and thunderstorms.

title: Landslide blocks Nan–Phayao Highway 1148
detail: Overnight rain brought mud and large trees across both lanes at km 73+250 (Sakoen–Sop Thu); heavy machinery was sent and detours set up, per The Nation.

title: Flooding shuts Highway 401 toward Phuket, tourists evacuated
detail: Floodwater made Highway 401 at km 66+600 impassable for small vehicles; DDPM evacuated stranded tourists in high-clearance trucks, and traffic was sent via Highway 4118, per Khaosod English.

title: Landslide blocks a lane of Highway 12 in Phetchabun
detail: Soil and rocks blocked one lane at km 373+400, per The Nation.

title: Landslide severs road in Phanom, Surat Thani
detail: A landslide cut the road between Ban Saphan Tao and Ban Khlong Phum Duang, leaving it impassable, per The Nation.
place: Ban Saphan Tao–Ban Khlong Phum Duang, Khlong Sok subdistrict

title: Landslide and flash flood hit Rural Road MS 3007, Khun Yuam
detail: Soil slid onto Rural Road MS 3007 between Ban Mae Sape Tai and Ban Mae Sape Nuea, per The Nation.
place: Rural Road MS 3007, Ban Mae Sape Tai–Ban Mae Sape Nuea

title: Flash floods damage bridge approaches in Wiang Haeng
detail: Landslides and flash floods damaged two bridge approaches and blocked village roads in Wiang Haeng district, per The Nation.

title: Track cable fire halts MRT Blue and Purple lines
detail: An electrical short in a power cable caused a fire between Tao Poon and Bang Pho around 12:30. BEM suspended services and ran shuttle buses, and normal service resumed on the morning of 21 September, per Thai PBS World. No injuries were reported.

title: Torrential rain floods Pattaya roads up to 1 m
detail: Water nearly 1 m deep made Pattaya Third Road, Sukhumvit near the Pattaya intersection and Railway Road impassable for small vehicles; dangerous sections were closed, per Pattaya Mail.
place: Pattaya Third Road, Sukhumvit Road, Railway Road

title: Highway 331 submerged in Si Racha, Pattaya streets flooded
detail: The Nation reported all lanes of Highway 331 flooded from the Pinthong 1 flyover to the Nong Kham interchange. Many Pattaya roads also flooded, stalling cars and motorcycles.

title: Heavy rain floods major roads across Bangkok and suburbs
detail: After up to 105.5mm of rain, roads including Vibhavadi Rangsit, Ngam Wong Wan, Chaeng Watthana, Ram Inthra and Phahonyothin flooded, causing standstill traffic, per The Nation.
place: Vibhavadi Rangsit Rd (Lak Si) and other roads
